macro.regime: Hawkish Fed Repricing Deepens (ISM 55.5 + JOLTS 7.52M) as Midterm Results Pend and Hormuz Re-Escalates
macro.narrative: As of the Tue Nov 3 US close, the hawkish-repricing case firmed further: September JOLTS job openings printed 7.52M, well above the 7.15M consensus and 7.08M prior, stacking on October's hot ISM Manufacturing beat (55.5) to push CME-implied/prediction-market odds of a December 25bp Fed HIKE to roughly 73% (Polymarket/Kalshi/CME FedWatch convergent), versus the cut debate markets were running in October. The RBA delivered its expected hike to 4.85% (5th of 2026, highest since 2008) but on a 6-3 split vote -- more dissent than the near-unanimous economist call implied, a modest dovish tell inside an otherwise hawkish global tightening backdrop. US midterm elections were held Nov 3; as of this run (07:02 SGT Wed, ~18:02 ET Tue) no official House/Senate calls had landed in verifiable sources, though pre-close prediction markets had priced a likely Democratic House with Republicans favored to hold the Senate, and equities traded calmly into the close (S&P +0.36% to 7568.92, Nasdaq +0.83% to 25372.01, VIX -1.51% to 20.83) consistent with a largely priced-in gridlock outcome -- CNBC flagged a live risk of contested results extending uncertainty, so this is not yet resolved. Monday's Hormuz-driven oil crash partially reversed/stalled Tuesday (Brent -0.33% to $104.42, WTI +0.31% to $96.76) after Iran reiterated the strait stays closed pending US sanctions relief, complicating the clean 'reopening' narrative the market had priced Monday. The hyperscaler/AI-capex credit-stress theme (record Oracle/Meta CDS, CCC spreads near 4-year highs) is carried forward unchanged from yesterday's verified read -- no fresh contradicting or confirming data located this run. The China rare-earth truce deadline (Announcement No. 70) is now 6 days from expiry (Nov 10) with still no superseding legal text published.
